newsitem.title: CHINA: TRADING IN SHUI HING SHARES SUSPENDED.
newsitem.headline: TRADING IN SHUI HING SHARES SUSPENDED.

text.p: Trading in shares of Shui Hing Co Ltd was suspended on Wednesday at the company's request pending an announcement, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange said.
The stock surged HK$4.60, or 42.59 percent, to HK$15.40 on volume of 550,000 shares worth HK$7.60 million at 11.04 a.m. (0304 gmt) on Wednesday when trading was suspended.

Shui Hing, a department store operator, said in late July that its 71 percent controlling shareholder Daniel Koo and his family was approached by third parties relating to acquiring a stake in the company but no decision had been made yet.
The parties included a group with a China background but it was not clear as to whether the talks would involve a change in control of the company, it had said.
Shui Hing officials were not immediately available to comment.
